coupling: In lib/mprintf.c, out_string() emits a %s argument either through a fast path (stream_run(), which trusts the precomputed length) or a bounded path (stream_zrun(), which stops at the string's NUL). The safety invariant is: the fast path is taken exactly when the precomputed length is exact. The first commit (431e990, 'avoid scanning strings twice') establishes that invariant across a widened domain: it extends the fast path from prec == -1 to all prec < 0 and, in the same breath, makes the length exact for every negative precision by changing the length branch to 'else if(prec >= 0)' so all negatives fall through to strlen(). Read alone it is internally consistent, output-equivalent, and safe (verified by execution: the intermediate tree formats the probe input cleanly). The second commit (3f2e9d3, 'tidy-up: miscellaneous') later folds the length branch back to 'else if(prec != -1)', on the plausible-but-wrong premise that a negative precision is normalized to -1 before output - that normalization only exists for the .* argument form (FLAGS_PRECPARAM, formatf), while an explicit '%.-Ns' parses via parse_flags' is_neg path into p.prec = -N and passes through unnormalized. Against the original dispatch (prec == -1) the fold is harmless: prec = -N still takes the NUL-bounded stream_zrun() path, so the fold alone changes nothing reachable. Only the composition is unsafe: prec = -N now yields len = (size_t)-N (~2^64) while the first commit's widened fast path (prec < 0 -> stream_run) trusts that length and emits it from a normal NUL-terminated string, producing a massive out-of-bounds read inside libcurl (ASan: heap-buffer-overflow in alloc_addrun) reachable from the public curl_maprintf() with an in-contract format string and argument. The defect is not contained in either commit's diff: reverting-to-safe requires knowing the other commit's assumption - the first commit's dispatch is only sound because of the length guard the second commit removed, and the second commit's fold is only unsound because of the dispatch the first commit widened - so a commit-by-commit reviewer sees two correct diffs and no single-commit repair follows from reading either diff in isolation; a correct fix must restore the invariant split across both (e.g. also normalize FLAGS_PREC negatives to -1, or keep the length exact for every precision value that can take the fast path).
